**About The Team**
 The Privacy Engineering Team at OpenAI is committed to integrating privacy as a foundational element in OpenAI's mission of advancing Artificial General Intelligence (AGI). Our focus is on all OpenAI products and systems handling user data, striving to uphold the highest standards of data privacy and security.
   

  

 We build essential production services, develop novel privacy\-preserving techniques, and equip cross\-functional engineering and research partners with the necessary tools to ensure responsible data use. Our approach to prioritizing responsible data use is integral to OpenAI's mission of safely introducing AGI that offers widespread benefits.
   

  

**About The Role**
 As a part of the Privacy Engineering Team, you will work on the frontlines of safeguarding user data while ensuring the usability and efficiency of our AI systems. You will help us understand and implement the latest research in privacy\-enhancing technologies such as differential privacy, federated learning, and data memorization. Moreover, you will focus on investigating the interaction between privacy and machine learning, developing innovative techniques to improve data anonymization, and preventing model inversion and membership inference attacks.
   

  

**This position is located in San Francisco. Relocation assistance is available.**
**In This Role, You Will**
* Design and prototype privacy\-preserving machine\-learning algorithms (e.g., differential privacy, secure aggregation, federated learning) that can be deployed at OpenAI scale.
* Measure and strengthen model robustness against privacy attacks such as membership inference, model inversion, and data memorization leaks—balancing utility with provable guarantees.
* Develop internal libraries, evaluation suites, and documentation that make cutting\-edge privacy techniques accessible to engineering and research teams.
* Lead deep\-dive investigations into the privacy–performance trade\-offs of large models, publishing insights that inform model\-training and product\-safety decisions.
* Define and codify privacy standards, threat models, and audit procedures that guide the entire ML lifecycle—from dataset curation to post\-deployment monitoring.
* Collaborate across Security, Policy, Product, and Legal to translate evolving regulatory requirements into practical technical safeguards and tooling.


**You Might Thrive In This Role If You**
* Have hands\-on research or production experience with PETs.
* Are fluent in modern deep\-learning stacks (PyTorch/JAX) and comfortable turning cutting\-edge papers into reliable, well\-tested code.
* Enjoy stress\-testing models—probing them for private data leakage—and can explain complex attack vectors to non\-experts with clarity.
* Have a track record of publishing (or implementing) novel privacy or security work and relish bridging the gap between academia and real\-world systems.
* Thrive in fast\-moving, cross\-disciplinary environments where you alternate between open\-ended research and shipping production features under tight deadlines.
* Communicate crisply, document rigorously, and care deeply about building AI systems that respect user privacy while pushing the frontiers of capability.

**Forward Deployed Engineer \| Palantir\-style FDE at a software holdco backed by the Collisons, General Catalyst \& D1 \| New York / SF / Toronto (Hybrid) \| $185K–$240K base** 




  





 We've partnered with a new kind of software holding company: one that buys great vertical\-market software businesses and holds them permanently, then grows them with agentic AI rather than financial engineering. They recently closed a $250M Series B from an exceptional roster, including General Catalyst, D1 Capital, CPMG, Sator Grove and the family offices of some of tech's most successful founders, among them Patrick and John Collison, Tony Xu, Eric Glyman and Karim Atiyeh. The founders have done it before: one a former President of Instacart, the other a former Sequoia partner. They run on permanent, committed capital with no pressure to sell, and one clear thesis, scale through software, not headcount.
 



  





 This is a rare Palantir\-style Forward Deployed Engineer role, and the leverage is unusual. You won't write decks. You'll drop into a company that already has customers and revenue, work out which two or three workflows agentic software can genuinely fix, then build it: integrations, prompts, evals, the interface people actually use. You ship it into live operations, tune the autonomy tiers until it runs without anyone hovering, and hand it off clean. Then you write down what you learned, and the next deployment in that vertical goes faster because you did the work first. The difference from selling software is that the customer is a company they own, so if it doesn't work, they feel it directly.
 



  





 The Role
 



  





 As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you will:
 



  





 Drop into a portfolio company, learn how it actually runs, earn the operators' trust, and find the two or three highest\-leverage workflows for agentic software.
 



 Build the wedge: the integrations, prompts, evals and UI to land the first agentic loop on the core platform.
 



 Operate and tune deployed systems after launch, adjusting autonomy tiers and handing off cleanly once stable.
 



 Act as the technical face to portfolio\-company GMs, setting expectations and making the system their leverage.
 



 Bring patterns back to HQ and codify them into playbooks that speed up every future deployment in the vertical.
 



  





 About You
 



  





 You have four to six years of experience, with three the absolute floor and we mean it. Big Tech alone won't clear the bar; the strongest profiles pair a recognisable company with real high\-growth startup experience.
 



 You have genuine tenure at a startup people have heard of, and stayed long enough to watch your own decisions play out. A string of sub\-year stints is the most common reason strong engineers get passed on here.
 



 You can own delivery solo, database through to screen: TypeScript or Python on the backend, React on the frontend, SQL. Specialists get blocked constantly in this role.
 



 You have shipped production LLM or agentic software that external users depended on, with evals, autonomy gating and outcome tracking, not prototypes or demos.
 



 You build with AI dev tools every day and have opinions about them, whether that's Cursor, Claude Code, Copilot or MCP servers. If you don't work this way, the pace will be uncomfortable.
 



 You have operator instincts: you can read a P\&L, sit with a GM who has never written code, disagree, be right, and leave with a scoped technical problem.
 



 You are based in or willing to relocate to New York, San Francisco or Toronto, comfortable with at least three days a week in office plus two to three days travelling to portfolio sites. Open to visa transfers including OPT and H\-1B, with relocation help.
 



  





 The interview will ask you to walk through the hardest technical decision you've made: the decision, the option you turned down, and why. Come ready to go three layers into something you built. The team is hiring several engineers and moving quickly. If you want to ship agentic software into live operations and own the outcomes across an entire portfolio, apply now or send your CV directly to will@inventurerecruitment.com.
